_comment: S2380 - the declared phone UI sweep, in the order it is taken. Mirrors the field set of
wear-prerelease-screens.json rather than generalising it (strategic ADR-2).
reach: resourceId is preferred over label EVERYWHERE, because the sweep runs in two languages
and a label is translated. Two places cannot use an id and say so in their own note: the four
SettingsActivity tabs (TabLayoutMediator builds them, a TabLayout.Tab carries no android:id) and
the MainActivity three-dots popup (MainProgramsMenuCoordinator adds items at runtime with
popup.menu.add(.., labelRes), and a PopupMenu row carries no resource-id).
expect: a token that is on the DESTINATION and not on the screen it was opened from. For a
popup-reached screen this rules out the popup item's OWN label - a tap that misses leaves the
popup open still showing that text, and the walk would record a screen it never opened.
expectRes: the string resource the token is matched against. The gate asserts the resource
resolves, that its CURRENT value contains `expect`, and that some file in the module renders it.
backAfter: BACK presses after the check, to return to a known position. 0 keeps the walk where
it is - used when the next entry opens from this screen.
optional: the entry may legitimately be absent; a missing control is `skipped`, not `unreachable`.
stateDependent: present only in some app states; same relief as optional but for a different cause.
secure: the surface sets FLAG_SECURE while settings.secureSensitiveScreens is on. `setup` turns
that setting off for the run, so these shoot normally; if a frame still comes back blank the
outcome is `manual` with the node tree beside it, never `failed`.
ownsOrientation: the surface drives its own orientation and does not follow a forced
user_rotation by design; the value is the reason. A frame whose pixels contradict the
combination's orientation is then `skipped` with that reason, not `manual`.
setup: run ONCE per run, before the first combination - not per combination. Nothing here
depends on orientation, theme or language, and the app state it builds is what makes roughly a
third of the catalog reachable at all (a seeded DEVICE is not a seeded APP: app_v2's resource
list starts empty). teardown restores what setup changed.
S2380 phase 03: `excluded` and the per-screen `expand` lists are added by step 03.3.

setup.name: Turn off secure sensitive screens

steps.label: @string/settings_tab_general
steps.note: Tab strip carries no id - see _comment.

Every collapsible section of General registers with defaultExpanded=false (GeneralSettingsFragment.setupCollapsibleSections), so the row below is not merely off-screen - it is inside a collapsed container and no amount of scrolling reveals it. The walk reported it as 'the row never became visible' (emulator-5554, 2026-09-20).

setup.note: Default ON (S1045). While on, the add-resource wizard and the resource editor return a black frame through BaseActivity.applySecureFlagIfEnabled, so four surfaces would be unphotographable. It is an app settings key, not a system one, and adb.ps1 prefs only reads - so the switch is thrown through the UI, which the walker can already do. teardown puts it back.

setup.name: Enable the Streams sub-program
setup.note: AppSettings.enableStreams defaults false, so without this the Streams entry is absent from the popup and StreamsActivity is never swept.

setup.name: Enable the sub-programs the popup menu offers
setup.note: Every entry below that opens from btnMainDropdownMenu except the quick-launch panel, Streams and the mirror is a sub-program that is OFF on a fresh install: the popup lists only what the registry reports available, so the calculator, stopwatch, both flashlights, the mini-game and the Wear companion were absent and scored unreachable (emulator-5562, 2026-09-25). The toggles run in layout order, because a toggle hunt scrolls down only.

setup.name: Configure one local resource over the seeded root
setup.note: Browse, the player, duplicates and the resource editor all open only from a configured resource row. Without this they would every one be excluded needs-seeded-content and the sweep would photograph the shell of the app rather than the app.

teardown.name: Turn secure sensitive screens back on

steps.note: Collapsed by default, exactly as in the setup entry above.

teardown.note: Research 03 residual risk: a run that dies mid-walk leaves the protection off. The walker re-asserts this at start of run as well as at end, so the next run repairs an abandoned one.

screens.name: Main - resource list
screens.note: Start destination; the app is already here after launch. The marker is the resource-type tab strip's id, which exists only on Main. It replaced the add-resource button's LABEL (add_resource_title): that label is drawn only while the button has room for it, so at 360 dp the button is icon-only and the walk refused every combination reporting that the app never reached its start screen while it was standing on it (emulator-5554, 2026-09-20). An id is neither translated nor width-dependent.

screens.name: Add resource wizard
screens.note: FLAG_SECURE via BaseActivity.applySecureFlagIfEnabled + isSensitiveScreen(); setup-disable-secure-screens makes it photographable.

screens.name: Companion QR scan
screens.expect: Point the camera at the companion QR code
screens.note: Opens the camera; the hint is drawn over the preview.

screens.name: Browse - resource contents
screens.label: @string/virtual_all_video
screens.note: The All Videos virtual resource, named rather than tapped at the list's centre: the centre tap opened All Music on one run and the player then had no Play/Pause to find. It lists the seeded videos through MediaStore, so the player below opens a video. The marker is the ops button's content description; Main's own cards carry no such node.

screens.name: Player - unified viewer
screens.ownsOrientation: By default the player follows the physical sensor (playerFollowSystemRotation=false, playerRotationSensorEnabled=true -> SCREEN_ORIENTATION_SENSOR, S0162), so a forced user_rotation with accelerometer rotation off does not rotate it; the emulator sensor reports portrait (S3537).
screens.note: tap-first-item taps the first row's file name (itemId), never the list's own id, whose centre is whatever sits there - a select checkbox on 2026-09-25. Reached from All Videos, so the row is a seeded video and the transport is drawn. The marker is the button's id: its description follows the playback state ("Play" or "Pause"), so play_pause never matches.

screens.name: Player - translation settings dialog
screens.note: The `translation` settings section lives here and nowhere else - it is not reachable from the Settings entry point. `translation_settings` is NOT the marker: it is the content description of the four host buttons on the player itself.

screens.name: Duplicates
screens.label: @string/action_find_duplicates
screens.note: Two taps: the ops button opens menu_resource_ops, the menu item starts the activity.

screens.name: Resource editor
screens.label: @string/edit
screens.note: The seeded resource's overflow menu, Edit item. The inline pencil (btnEdit in layoutInlineActions) is not drawn on a 360 dp list, and the FIRST overflow on Main belongs to a virtual resource, so the opener is named by the description that carries the seeded row's path. FLAG_SECURE like the wizard; the title is set on the toolbar for ResourceEditorMode.EDIT.

screens.name: Settings
screens.note: Marker is a tab title rather than the screen title, because `settings` ("Settings") is also the label of the button on Main that opens it.

screens.name: Settings - General tab
screens.label: @string/settings_tab_general
screens.note: Tab, not a row: TabLayoutMediator builds the strip and a tab carries no android:id. The four tab labels are the reason the language dimension changes only between whole catalog passes.

expand.note: Drawn only in a debug build, which is what the sweep runs.

screens.name: Settings - Media tab
screens.label: @string/settings_tab_media
screens.note: The tab's own container has no unique static string of its own; the marker is taken from the first sub-page, which the container attaches on expand.

expand.note: Drawn only in the vr flavor; the sweep runs standard, so this node is expected to be `skipped` and that is not a defect.

screens.expandNote: The other seven headers in this container - Images, Video, Audio, Documents, Other, Streams, Broadcast - are not expand nodes: each attaches its own child fragment and is walked as a screen record of its own above. S3078 moved Broadcast out of this list: S2817 gave it fragment_settings_broadcast with seven declared settings rows, so the header is no longer the only static token it has.

screens.name: Settings - Media - Audio
screens.note: A collapsible section inside one long NestedScrollView, not a separate screen; the child fragment is attached lazily on expand.

screens.name: Settings - Media - Streams
screens.note: The section header's own string is settings_streams_section, so the toggle inside it is the marker rather than the header that is visible before opening.

screens.name: Settings - Media - Broadcast
screens.note: The section header's own string is settings_broadcast_section, so the toggle inside it is the marker rather than the header that is visible before opening. Drawn by the three flavors that mount src/broadcastSource, which includes the standard flavor the sweep runs.

screens.name: Settings - Player tab
screens.label: @string/settings_tab_playback
screens.note: The tab renders "Player", not "Playback" - the resource key and the drawn text diverge, so the walker must resolve the label through the resource, never from the key name.

screens.name: Settings - Management tab
screens.label: @string/settings_tab_operations
screens.note: Drawn as "Management"; its layout is still named fragment_settings_destinations and the settings manifest still calls the section `destinations`.

expand.note: The only section whose body carries no string resource of its own - every row inside it is built at runtime from the share-target registry - so this node's token is the header's own title and it proves presence rather than expansion.

screens.name: Settings - Stopwatch dialog
screens.note: The dialog's title is set programmatically, so the marker is a row inside it. StopwatchActivity opens the same dialog from btnStopwatchSettings; it is walked here, from settings, so the sweep does not photograph one surface twice.

screens.name: Settings - Scheduled operations screen
screens.note: S3365: the link row opens the standalone program screen that took over the extracted card; the sweep photographs it from its settings entry point so the row and the screen are covered together.

screens.name: Settings - Launcher dialog
screens.note: launcher_settings_dialog_title is NOT the marker - it is also the label of the row that opens it.

screens.name: Settings - Launcher reset confirmation
screens.expect: System launcher settings will be reset
screens.note: A destructive confirmation. The walk photographs it and leaves by BACK - it never presses the confirm button.

screens.name: Controls and keybindings
screens.note: The resource value is "Controls & Keybindings"; the token is the tail so the ampersand's XML escaping never enters the comparison.

screens.name: Statistics
screens.note: The row is drawn only while AppSettings.enableStatistics is on, which is its default.

screens.name: Wear companion
screens.label: @string/wear_companion
screens.expect: Push network resources to your connected Wear OS watch.
screens.note: Popup item, so label rather than id. The marker is drawn by the Compose island WearCompanionScreen, not by the activity's XML shell - the shell carries only the popup item's own title.

screens.name: Wear resource selection
screens.label: @string/wear_resource_selection_title
screens.note: wear_resource_selection_title is the opening button's own label on the parent, so a row inside the screen is the marker instead.

screens.name: Calculator
screens.label: @string/app_launch_panel_route_calculator
screens.expect: Tap to copy, long-press to paste a number
screens.note: The popup item is the route label app_launch_panel_route_calculator, drawn only after setup-enable-programs; the display's content description is the marker.

screens.name: Mirror
screens.label: @string/mirror_title
screens.note: Opens the front camera full screen; the close button's content description is the only static string on it.

screens.name: Water flashlight
screens.label: @string/water_flashlight_title
screens.note: The screen is deliberately deaf to touch, so BACK is the only exit and the walker must not try to tap its way out.

screens.name: Mini-game
screens.label: @string/app_launch_panel_route_game
screens.note: The popup item is the route label app_launch_panel_route_game ("Mini-game") and the screen reads its own title, so the two do not collide. Drawn only after setup-enable-programs switches the game on.

screens.name: Quick launch panel
screens.label: @string/app_launch_panel_title
screens.note: The activity is a transparent host; the panel itself is a dialog fragment. app_launch_panel_title is both the popup item and the panel's own title, so the edit action is the marker.

screens.name: Streams
screens.label: @string/streams_title
screens.note: Present only after setup-enable-streams. streams_title is the popup item's label, so the search hint is the marker.

screens.name: Camera capture
screens.label: @string/widget_camera_quick_capture_label
screens.note: The popup item is the route label widget_camera_quick_capture_label ("Quick capture"); the mode toggle on the screen reads "Photo".

screens.name: Camera settings dialog
screens.note: The `camera` settings section is covered here. It is not reachable from the Settings entry point: CameraSettingsDialogFragment has exactly one call site, the gear button on the capture screen. camera_settings_title is NOT the marker - it is the content description of that same gear button on the host screen. The section's second layout, dialog_camera_ocr_settings, belongs to CameraOcrTranslateActivity, which is excluded no-static-marker; the section stays covered by this entry.

excluded.note: First-run onboarding, started from MainActivity before the main graph is usable. The sweep runs against an app that has already been through it.

activity_system_info.xml carries the toolbar title - which is also the popup item's own label - three buttons on the shared copy/save/share strings, and an empty ScrollView filled at runtime. Nothing on it can distinguish 'opened' from 'popup still showing'.
activity_black_screen.xml is a single FrameLayout with a black background and no child views. There is nothing to assert and nothing to photograph.

Its content container is an empty FrameLayout filled at runtime; the only static string sits in a fallback group that is visible ONLY while the sub-program is disabled, so it proves the opposite of an open screen.
Three mutually exclusive states - result, crop, loading - with no string common to all of them, so no token proves the screen opened rather than that it landed in one particular state.

The content it needs is a LIVE microphone session: the screen renders a descriptor the Live state carries, and reaching it means opening the microphone and broadcasting for the length of the sweep. That is a side effect a UI sweep must not have - the same call the watch walk made for WearBroadcastQrScreen.

excludedSurfaces.note: The fourth FLAG_SECURE surface, and the only one that is not an activity. It sets the flag by its own path rather than through BaseActivity, and it opens only while authorizing a real remote source - a live account the sweep does not have. Named here so all four secure surfaces are accounted for: two carry `secure: true` on their screen record, CompanionQrShareActivity is in `excluded`, and this one is here.

excludedSettingsSections.note: Not a phone settings page: a single entry belonging to a Network Monitor tool tab, reached from its own activity, which is itself excluded no-static-marker.
Four Compose screens that live in the wear module and render no app_v2 resource. Strategic 3.2 puts Wear OS out of scope entirely; the watch has its own walk.

_coverage: Activities: dev/ACTIVITY_CATALOG/app_v2.jsonl holds 60 records. 24 are walked by the `screens` list
above (some screens are dialogs hosted by an already-counted activity, so screens > activities),
and 36 are named in `excluded`. 24 + 36 = 60, with no record in both lists and none in neither.
Settings sections: docs/settings/settings-manifest.json holds 17 distinct sectionId values.
16 are covered by a walk entry - 9 as settings pages, 7 as dialogs and screens, two of those
seven (camera, translation) from their host screen rather than from the settings entry, because
no settings path to them exists. 2 are named in `excludedSettingsSections`. 16 + 2 = 18.
The step 03.4 gate re-derives both sums from the source files rather than trusting this note.
